subject: SOC 2 Type II — clarification on coverage dates and point-in-time evidence
messages:
From: Samira Khan <audit@clarityaudits.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Ben Riley <ben.riley@acmeproducts.com>
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: SOC 2 Type II — scope / cutoff clarifications

Hi Connor,

Quick question from the audit team as we prepare the SOC 2 Type II report request for Acme: could you confirm exactly which monthly periods your current report covers? The request from procurement lists "Q4 2025 - Q3 2026 (inclusive)" but the SOC 2 cover letter we received referenced a 12-month period ending 2026-09-30. We need to reconcile the months so our review plan picks the right sample windows.

Also: for point-in-time items (daily backups, configuration snapshots, and environment variables), do you have a documented cutoff time we should treat as the snapshot date? If your report is point-in-time at month-end vs. a daily snapshot, that changes what evidence the auditors will request.

Can you share the exact start/end dates you consider "covered" by the current SOC 2 Type II and whether you treat evidence claims as "month-end inclusive" or as specific day/time snapshots?

Appreciate the quick turn — procurement is aiming to finalize next-week.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Senior Auditor | Clarity Audits

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Riley <ben.riley@acmeproducts.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — scope / cutoff clarifications

Hi Samira — thanks for the ping. Short answer: our latest SOC 2 Type II report covers the 12-month period from 2025-10-01 through 2026-09-30 (inclusive). We generally treat "coverage" as inclusive of the start and end dates reported in the SOC 2 cover page.

A few clarifying points to avoid downstream confusion:
- "Month-inclusive" statements in procurement templates are ambiguous: we report a continuous 12-month testing period (Oct 1 2025 -> Sep 30 2026). If a customer asks for "Q4 2025 - Q3 2026 (inclusive)", that maps to the same 12 months, but we prefer explicit ISO dates to avoid off-by-one errors.
- For operational evidence: most of our controls are assessed as "period-based" (logs, change windows) but certain artifacts (backups, a configuration export) are produced as daily snapshots. Our auditors typically accept period-based sampling plus specific point-in-time exports for items that are not continuously stored.

If you need formal artifacts for point-in-time proof, we can provide:
1) a timestamped S3 export of the infrastructure configuration as of 2026-09-30 23:59:59 UTC,
2) an aggregated log snapshot for that day (rotations applied), and
3) the SOC 2 period matrix that maps controls to sample windows.

Neha — can you confirm the exact filenames and whether we have a preferred timezone for the official snapshot (we usually record UTC but procurement sometimes requests vendor local TZ). Vivek — FYI in case we need to route this to Dedicated/Private infra owners for precise exports.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi Samira — following up with the artifacts. Attached are two small stubs: a SOC 2 period matrix (redwood_soc2_period_matrix.pdf) that lists start/end dates and control sample windows, and a text snapshot of the log export for 2026-09-30 (log_snapshot_20261120.txt) that shows the UTC timestamp header used by our retention process.

To confirm the answers to your earlier questions:
- The monthly/month-end exports are part of our retention process but full S3 configuration snapshots are taken daily and retained for 90 days; auditors typically accept the month-end snapshot for testing when combined with log sampling.
- Official snapshot timezone: UTC. The files we provided are labeled with UTC timestamps.
- We produce these exports on an ongoing schedule (automated daily jobs) and can regenerate the specific timestamped export on request for audit reproducibility.

If you need the exports ingested into a specific secure share (SFTP or Acme's Box), let me know and I'll arrange transfer with Ops.
